title: What Happens to Bank Accounts When Someone Passes Away Without a Will
bigPicture: When there is no will, the bank freezes the account and the state decides who gets the money based on family ties.
whatYouNeedToKnow: The bank will freeze the account once it learns of the death — no one can withdraw money yet.
Each state has rules that decide who gets the money, usually starting with a spouse or children.
Joint accounts often pass directly to the surviving owner, bypassing the freeze.
Smaller accounts may have a simpler process than large ones.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Trying to withdraw money before the bank clears it — this can cause legal trouble.
Assuming the money automatically goes to one family member without checking state rules.
Waiting too long to notify the bank, which can delay everything.
actionSteps: Get certified copies of the death certificate.
Call the bank and let them know the person has passed away.
Ask the bank what documents they need next.
Talk to a local estate attorney if the process feels overwhelming.
